newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond new issuance continues brisk pace.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond new issuance continues brisk pace.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds players continued their focus on the primary market on Thursday as new deal issuance continued at a brisk pace.

In the investment grade sector, where issuance has been particularly heavy, traders reported some price weakness in the secondary market as many investors were selling their older bonds to particapte in the new offerings.
Junk traders said prices in the secondary market were generally steady, despite the new supply.
"New supply is reasonably heavy but not overwhelming. It hasn't depressed prices," said one high-yield trader.
McDonnell Douglas was expected to tap the market with a $250 million debt deal through Merrill Lynch & Co later on Thursday, according to market sources.

Earlier in the day, Tribune Co sold $250 million in 10-year notes through Merrill; Norwest Financial sold $150 mllion in five-year notes through Merrill; and Apache Corp sold $150 million in 100-year debentures through Goldman Sachs & Co Inc.
Traders said spreads on $500 million of debentures sold by Ford Motor Co at 77 basis points over Treasuries on Wednesday widened by five basis points in Thursday's trade.
In the high-yield market, Outsourcing Solutions was expected to sell $100 million in senior subordinated notes in a 144a private placement through Goldman on Thursday, according to market sources.
Goldman was also expected to price a $175 million 144a offering of senior subordinated notes by Forcenergy Inc FBAS.O on Thursday, syndicate officials said.
Intertek Finance plc issued $203 million in 10.25 percent 10-year notes in a 144A deal through BT Securities Corp on Thursday.
Traders say Pricellular 10 3/4 percent bonds, which were priced at par on Wednesday, were bid at par and 7/8 in Thursday's trade, an indication of continued strong demand for the deal.
